summary: Add visual trend summaries and written exam practice for Period 3 radii, melting points and conductivity.

improvements.where: note, after the Melting point paragraph in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: Outcome 9701-9.1.1 asks learners to indicate the periodicity of melting point, including the silicon peak and the phosphorus-to-sulfur reversal; the note has no diagram.
improvements.what: Use graph_sketch for a qualitative melting-point graph with Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl and Ar in order; show the maximum at Si, the sharp fall to P, the rise to S and the fall through Cl to Ar. Add a short note caption linking each segment to metallic, giant covalent, simple molecular or monatomic structure.

improvements.where: note, after the Ionic radius paragraph in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: Outcome 9701-9.1.1 requires the ionic-radius trend; a graph makes the discontinuity between cations and anions clearer than the current prose alone.
improvements.what: Use graph_sketch with two separate decreasing series: Na+ to Mg2+ to Al3+, and P3- to S2- to Cl-. Label the cation-to-anion gap explicitly, and omit Si rather than joining the two series into one smooth line.

improvements.why: Existing generated and selected past items are all MCQs, so learners never practise writing the structure, attraction overcome and causal comparison that the structured-paper examiner report says was often missing.
improvements.what: Add one short or structured Explain question comparing Si and S melting, crediting giant covalent Si–Si bonds versus intermolecular instantaneous dipole–induced dipole attractions between S8 molecules. Add one written Explain comparison of Mg and Si conductivity, crediting mobile delocalised electrons in Mg and semiconductor behavior in covalently bonded Si. Give markable rubric/scheme and specific progressive hints.

improvements.why: The outcome uses Describe, but all selected past-paper items are MCQs and the generated Describe items are also MCQs.
improvements.what: Add a short written Describe item asking for the Period 3 melting-point trend from Na to Ar, with scheme points for rise to Si, fall to P, rise to S, then fall through Cl to Ar; do not credit a monotonic decline after Si.

improvements.why: Their three hints are the same generic text even when the question is about different physical properties, limiting their value in tutoring.
improvements.what: Add property-specific hints to new questions and, where additive content is possible, supplementary teaching-card discover prompts that ask learners to predict the radius jump, Si melting peak, and metal-to-Si conductivity change before revealing the explanation.
